newsitem.title: USA: Toyota unveils electric car, the RAV4-EV.
newsitem.headline: Toyota unveils electric car, the RAV4-EV.

text.p: Toyota Motor Sales, USA Inc Thursday unveiled its RAV4-EV electric vehicle, a member of the popular sport utility class of cars, set for sale in mid-October.
Suggested retail price is $42,000. The lease price will be $499 per month for 36 months with no mileage restrictions, the U.S.-based wing of Japanese auto maker Toyota Motor Corp said in a statement.
The RAV4-EV is identical in size and shape to Toyota's four-door RAV sport utility automobiles currently being sold, and features folding rear seats, power windows and door locks.

For power, the RAV4-EV uses nickel-metal hydride batteries and reaches speeds up to 79 miles per hour with a city/highway range of 120 miles. The batteries charge on standard equipment, and the car carries its own components, obviating the need for additional equipment purchases.

"We began our electric vehicle program with extensive in-house testing, moved to real-world driving with test-fleet partners, and are now ready to make production vehicles available to fleet buyers," said Dave Illingworth, general manager of the Toyota U.S. division. "We fully believe that this is the finest full-electric vehicle produced today."
California mandates 10 percent of all vechicles sold in the state by manufacturers must be non-polluting, zero-emission vechicles by 2003.
General Motors Corp recently launched its electric vehicle, called the EV-1.
Toyota is targeting fleet sales to commercial users and businesses with the RAV4-EV. It expects initial sales to concentrate in California and the northeastern United States.
It believes the majority of vehicles will be leased rather than purchased. Incentives and purchase assistance programs up to $9,000 are available through local and federal agencies.
